conversation.assistant:
That’s a good problem to have—it usually means you used enough glue rather than too little. And it sounds like the box itself came together very well.

On the glue: wiping it while it’s wet is the one thing that tends to cause those smear marks. It spreads the glue into the grain, and that can show up later when you apply a finish (you’ll get lighter patches where the finish won’t absorb properly).

It’s not ruined at all—you’ve just got a little cleanup to do.

Best practice for next time:
- Apply a thin, even layer of glue (you don’t need much)
- Clamp the joint
- Let the squeeze-out sit for about 10–20 minutes until it turns rubbery
- Then lift it off with a chisel or even your fingernail—it’ll peel away cleanly

For your current box:
- Let everything dry completely
- Then lightly plane or sand the affected areas

Your plane is actually perfect for this if the smears are on flat surfaces—just take very light passes. You’ll remove the glue and leave a clean surface. Sanding works too, just a bit less precise.

Before finishing, a good check is:
- Wipe the wood lightly with a damp cloth (just water)
- Any glue spots will show up as dull or lighter patches

If you see any, clean those areas up a bit more.

For the bottom panel, you’re in a nice straightforward phase:
- Cut it to match the outside dimensions of the box
- Make sure the box is sitting flat (no twist)
- Glue and clamp it on, or glue plus a few small nails if you like

You’re past the hardest part, honestly. This is where it starts to feel like a real object.
